findings.claim: The row's own intra-verse doubling claim names skeleton tier for a pair that matches one tier higher, at accent_stripped.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale states 'the watchman noun repeats at skeleton tier while the night-forms that follow it differ at every tier'. Spliced from MT 21:11, the two watchman nouns are "שֹׁמֵר֙" (token 6) and "שֹׁמֵ֖ר" (token 9): consonants and vowel points are identical and only the cantillation differs (U+0599 borne after the resh in the first, U+0596 borne on the mem in the second), so they collate accent_stripped-equal, i.e. the strongest matching tier is accent_stripped, not skeleton. The paired claim about the night-forms is correct: "מִלַּ֔יְלָה" and "מִלֵּֽיל" collate at no tier against each other. Under the tier-disclosure standard the named tier must be the collate truth, and byte / accent_stripped / skeleton are never conflated.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'repeats at skeleton tier' with 'repeats at accent_stripped tier — consonants and vowel points identical, cantillation differs' in boundary_rationale. Field repair only; the seam warrant (the verse-initial massa header at oshb:Isa.21.11) is untouched and no span change follows.

findings.claim: The row's declared opening driver is an in-that-day scene shift resting on a formula that is not verse-initial at the cited verse and that recurs byte-identically across the row's own seams, none of it disclosed; the immediately preceding shipped row argues the opposite about this same formula at this same seam.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'opens the unit on an explicit in-that-day scene shift', and observed_substrate_signals leads with oracle_frame.scene_shift, so the day formula is the declared operative signal. Spliced from source, MT 22:12 opens "וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" — the formula "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" is the fifth and sixth words, not verse-initial. The same formula stands at MT 22:8 as "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא" (four verses back, inside the immediately preceding row's span Isa.22.1-Isa.22.11), collating accent_stripped-equal against the MT 22:12 form, and at MT 22:20 as the tail of "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא", where it is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the MT 22:12 form, and again verse-initially at MT 22:25 (accent_stripped against MT 22:12). The row discloses none of these recurrences. The immediately preceding row's device_notes rules on this exact seam that 'The in-that-day formula itself is cross-seam cohesion rather than a boundary driver ... it is verse-initial at neither of the two sites bordering this row's own seam. The warrant for the cut rests instead on the fresh grammatical subject entering at oshb:Isa.22.12' — a warrant this row's observed_substrate_signals does not carry.
findings.proposed_change: Re-declare the operative opening signal as the fresh divine grammatical subject entering at oshb:Isa.22.12 (the finite verb with the stacked title as its subject, the first such in the header-bounded oracle), matching the preceding row's ruling; demote the in-that-day formula to disclosed cross-seam cohesion naming oshb:Isa.22.8 (accent_stripped), oshb:Isa.22.20 (byte) and oshb:Isa.22.25 (accent_stripped); add oshb:Isa.22.8 to boundary_evidence_refs; swap the lead observed_substrate_signals key off oracle_frame.scene_shift accordingly, and re-open confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative as dependent fields of the driver swap. Span Isa.22.12-Isa.22.14 unchanged; no span change proposed.

findings.claim: The row's closing-seam warrant — that the following verse opens on its own addressee shift and is a verse-initial addressee-specific commission — is byte-false: MT 22:20 carries no imperative, no vocative and no second-person form at all, and the addressee is unchanged across the seam.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'The row stops before the following verse's own in-that-day summons of a different, newly named servant, which opens the next unit on its own addressee shift'; device_notes: 'the cut still stands on the verse-initial addressee-specific commission opening the following verse, naming a different steward for installation rather than removal.' Spliced from source, MT 22:20 reads "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ": the newly named steward is governed by the prefixed preposition as the object of the first-person verb, and the verse contains zero second-person forms. It is therefore neither a commission nor an addressee shift — contrast this row's own opening at MT 22:15, whose commission is carried by the imperatives "לֶךְ בֹּא֙". The addressee is in fact unchanged across the seam: the 2ms chain closing this row's span, "וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ" (oshb:Isa.22.19, byte tier), resumes one verse past the seam at "כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙" (oshb:Isa.22.21, byte tier). The row states this counter-fact itself in device_notes ('A second-person-masculine-singular address chain crosses this unit's own closing seam ... resumes the direct address'), so the row contradicts itself; and the neighbouring shipped row that owns MT 22:20 reads the same bytes correctly, as a referent brought in 'as the object of the divine verb rather than as a fresh addressee', with 'the grammatical addressee carried over from the removal oracle ... still the one addressed one verse later'. The row ships at high confidence and observed_substrate_signals carries oracle_frame.addressee_shift.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the closing-seam warrant with the two signals that do stand in MT 22:20's own bytes and that the neighbouring row already argues: the verse-initial day-formula scene onset and the fresh named referent entering as the object of the divine verb rather than as a fresh addressee. Strike 'addressee shift' and 'addressee-specific commission' from the closing-seam prose; retain oracle_frame.addressee_shift only for this row's OPENING at oshb:Isa.22.15, whose imperatives do carry it; add oshb:Isa.22.20 to boundary_evidence_refs (only oshb:Isa.22.21 is presently carried for that side). As a driver swap this re-opens confidence, strongest_rejected_alternative and observed_substrate_signals. The seam itself survives on the replacement warrant, so no span change is proposed.
